transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm doing alright, thank you for asking. I do have a few questions about my recovery. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
According to our guidelines, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, please remember to be gentle and avoid straining your eyes. Also, be careful not to get any water in your eyes while gardening, especially in the first month after surgery. 

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. I appreciate it. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You should have been using preservative-free eye drops, not gel, to help with dryness. It's recommended to use these drops four times a day to start. If you're running low, you can get more from your GP or pharmacist. Remember to store your medication as directed. 

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Yes, I have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after surgery as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and just seems brighter than usual, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're outside. However, if it's severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to assess it further. 

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?
transcript.delivered: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after surgery as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and just seems brighter than usual, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. If you've only had one eye done, it's also normal to feel a bit "off balance" - this should improve once you have both eyes done.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions about your cataract surgery recovery. If you have any more questions or concerns, don't hesitate to reach out to your care team. They'll be happy to help. .
